headline: EU Accuses TikTok of Failing to Protect Minors' Privacy
summary: The European Commission says TikTok's default settings expose minors' accounts and content too widely, potentially leading to unwanted contact and cyberbullying.
details: The European Commission (EC) has sent TikTok its preliminary findings, accusing the platform of not meeting the safety standards required under the Digital Services Act (DSA). The EC stated that minors can set their accounts to public by default, allowing anyone to see their content.

The commission highlighted concerns that TikTok's algorithm recommends content from users aged 16-17 to its 'For You' feed. This could expose minors to unwanted contact, cyberbullying, or predatory behavior, as platforms accessible to minors must ensure a high level of privacy and safety.

TikTok faces a potential fine of up to six percent of its gross annual revenue if found non-compliant. The EC recommended that TikTok change the default settings for minors' accounts to be visible only to friends and stop recommending content from minor accounts.

This is not the first time TikTok has faced scrutiny from the EC. Earlier this year, the platform was accused of employing addictive design features. Additionally, the UK's Ofcom has also stated that TikTok is not effective enough at preventing harmful content from reaching children.
caption:
TikTok is under fire from the EU for failing to protect minors' privacy. The platform could face a massive fine.

The European Commission (EC) has sent TikTok its preliminary findings, accusing the platform of not meeting the safety standards required under the Digital Services Act (DSA). The EC stated that minors can set their accounts to public by default, allowing anyone to see their content.

The commission highlighted concerns that TikTok's algorithm recommends content from users aged 16-17 to its 'For You' feed. This could expose minors to unwanted contact, cyberbullying, or predatory behavior, as platforms accessible to minors must ensure a high level of privacy and safety.

TikTok faces a potential fine of up to six percent of its gross annual revenue if found non-compliant. The EC recommended that TikTok change the default settings for minors' accounts to be visible only to friends and stop recommending content from minor accounts.

This is not the first time TikTok has faced scrutiny from the EC. Earlier this year, the platform was accused of employing addictive design features. Additionally, the UK's Ofcom has also stated that TikTok is not effective enough at preventing harmful content from reaching children.
